title: Coffee Production and Sustainability: Linking Plant Responses, Crop Management and Value Chains
content: Coffee production faces interacting environmental, biological, and socioeconomic pressures that threaten yield stability and producer livelihoods. This review integrates scientific literature, international databases, and sectoral reports to examine how plant responses, crop management, and global value chains shape coffee sustainability. Climate variability, water limitation, vapor pressure deficit, and soil constraints affect physiological performance, while recurrent pest and disease damage generates cumulative losses across production cycles. These pressures interact with market volatility, unequal value distribution, and increasing requirements for traceability and deforestation-free sourcing, particularly challenging smallholder producers. Genetic improvement, integrated pest and disease management, improved soil management, and diversified production systems offer complementary adaptation pathways. However, the benefits of agroforestry and organic management depend on environmental conditions, system design, and available resources, with trade-offs affecting productivity and adoption. Sustaining coffee production therefore requires locally adapted strategies that combine crop resilience and resource efficiency with institutional support and more equitable participation in value chains. Coordinated investment in breeding, extension, and governance is essential to improve producers’ capacity to respond to environmental and market change.
